docs.title: Drone Battery Monte Carlo
docs.text:
This project compares drone battery options using a Monte Carlo simulation model under varying mission conditions (e.g., payload, wind, and temperature). It includes:

  • A simulation engine that estimates energy use and mission success
  • A desktop GUI for running comparisons and viewing plots
  • Published API documentation generated by Doxygen

docs.title: Summary (What the code does)
docs.text:
This code simulates the same drone mission many times while randomly varying key environmental and mission conditions. Each trial estimates how much energy the drone would use and whether the battery can complete the mission while still meeting a required safety reserve.

Instead of assuming “one average scenario,” the Monte Carlo approach produces a distribution of outcomes (best-case, typical, worst-case) so you can compare battery choices more realistically.

docs.title: Battery chemistry (what “Li-ion vs LiPo” means in the model)
docs.text:
The simulator compares two battery chemistries/form factors (example: Li-ion (NMC cylindrical) vs LiPo (pouch high-power)) by giving each battery its own performance parameters:

  • Nominal capacity (Wh): stored energy available at room temperature
  • Baseline power (W): typical cruise power draw with no extra load
  • Payload penalty: added power draw per lb of payload
  • Wind penalty: added power draw per mph of headwind
  • Cold capacity penalty: capacity reduction per °F below 70°F
  • Cold power penalty: power increase per °F below 70°F

In other words: “chemistry” differences are represented by different parameter values that reflect typical strengths/weaknesses (energy density, power delivery, cold performance, etc.).

docs.title: Factors varied per trial (stochastic inputs)
docs.text:
Each Monte Carlo trial samples a new set of conditions, then recomputes mission energy:

  • Wind (mph)
  • Temperature (°F)
  • Payload (lb)
  • Distance factor (multiplier on nominal mission distance)

Two modes are supported: - Nominal mode: uniform sampling across realistic ranges - Extreme mode: triangular sampling biased toward harsher conditions (stronger wind, colder temps, heavier payload, longer distance)

docs.title: Mission energy calculation (per trial)
docs.text: For each battery and trial: 1. Compute trial distance distance = nominal_distance * distance_factor 2. Compute power draw power = base_power + payload_penalty*payload + wind_penalty*wind 3. Apply cold effects (if temp < 70°F) - reduce effective capacity - increase power draw 4. Compute flight time time = distance / cruise_speed 5. Compute required energy energy_required (Wh) = power * time 6. Determine success with safety reserve Success if energy_required <= (effective_capacity * (1 - reserve_fraction))

docs.title: Statistical outputs (what “Monte Carlo results” mean)
docs.text:
After running many trials, the code summarizes results per battery using distribution statistics:

  • Success probability (%): fraction of trials that meet reserve requirement
  • Remaining energy (%): distribution of energy left at end of mission
  • Mean remaining
  • 5th percentile (P5): “near worst-case” remaining energy
  • 95th percentile (P95): “near best-case” remaining energy
  • Operational averages: average miles and payload across trials (and across successful trials)
  • Energy use metrics:
  • Average Wh per mission
  • Missions per charge: estimated missions possible before hitting reserve
  • Deliveries per charge: a conservative integer version (floor)

The GUI also plots histograms of remaining energy so you can visually compare distributions (spread, overlap, tail risk) between chemistries.

docs.title: GUI
docs.text: The project includes a desktop GUI (Tkinter + matplotlib) that lets you run Monte Carlo simulations and compare two battery configurations across typical and extreme mission conditions.

docs.title: 1) Simulation
docs.text:
Run the standard Monte Carlo simulation to compare Battery A vs Battery B under nominal sampling assumptions. The GUI produces:

  • Text summary of results (success rate, remaining energy stats, operational averages)
  • Distribution plots (remaining energy histograms)

docs.title: 2) Parameters Summary
docs.text: Shows the active parameters and model settings used during the run (battery parameters, mission config, penalties, and sampling ranges).

docs.title: 3) Extreme Conditions
docs.text: Runs a deliberately biased Monte Carlo intended to stress the mission (high wind, low temperature, high payload, and slightly longer distance).

docs.title: Extreme simulation settings
docs.text:
• Number of runs per battery (example shown: 500)
  • Biases:
  • Wind: high-biased (10–20 mph)
  • Temp: low-biased (10–95 °F)
  • Payload: high-biased (2.5–5 lb)
  • Distance factor: high-biased (1.0–1.1)

docs.text:
• Δ Mean remaining (Li-ion - LiPo): +2.66%

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: This page captures the system/model requirements for the Drone Battery Monte Carlo model and how each requirement is evaluated.

docs.title: REQ-001 — Mission Energy Use Under Variable Conditions
Requirement
docs.text: The model shall estimate battery energy draw per mission as a function of payload weight, flight distance, ambient temperature, and wind conditions.

docs.title: Assumptions / Constraints
docs.text:
• The drone follows a defined mission profile.
  • Empty drone weight is fixed at 50 lb for all simulation runs.
  • Cruise speed is fixed at 25 mph.
  • Payload varies from 0–5 lb.
  • Wind, temperature, payload, and distance factor are sampled stochastically.
  • Distance is modeled as:
  • nominal mission distance = 15 mi
  • distance factor = 0.9–1.1 nominal, or 1.0–1.1 in extreme mode
  • Battery performance is affected by:
  • baseline power draw
  • fixed drone-weight penalty
  • payload penalty
  • wind penalty
  • cold-weather power increase
  • cold-weather effective-capacity reduction
  • A 10% safety reserve is required.

docs.title: Question(s) Answered
docs.text:
• How much energy does a mission consume under varying operating conditions?
  • Which operational factors most affect mission battery draw?

docs.title: Primary Variables
docs.text:
• Payload Weight
  • Flight Distance
  • Ambient Temperature
  • Wind Speed
  • Battery Configuration

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Monte Carlo analysis
  • Randomly generate mission/environmental inputs
  • Compute:
  • mission distance
  • power draw
  • energy required
  • effective capacity
  • remaining energy
  • mission success/failure versus reserve threshold

docs.title: Outputs / Acceptance Evidence
docs.text:
• Energy used per mission (Wh)
  • Effective battery capacity (Wh)
  • Remaining energy after mission (Wh, %)
  • Success/failure against reserve threshold
  • Distribution statistics:
  • mean remaining energy
  • 5th percentile remaining energy
  • 95th percentile remaining energy

docs.title: Validation Data Source
docs.text:
• Battery test data
  • Engineering assumptions for power and temperature sensitivity
  • Simulation consistency checks

docs.title: Analysis Deliverable
docs.text:
• Plot/table of remaining energy distribution
  • Summary statistics for mission energy use
  • Sensitivity discussion for payload, distance, temperature, and wind

docs.title: REQ-002 — Mission Feasibility and Deliveries per Charge
Requirement
docs.text: The model shall determine whether a candidate battery can complete a mission profile and estimate the number of missions per charge under variable operating conditions.

docs.title: Assumptions / Constraints
docs.text:
• The drone follows a fixed cruise speed of 25 mph.
  • Empty drone weight is fixed at 50 lb.
  • Payload varies from 0–5 lb.
  • Mission distance varies around the nominal 15 mi baseline.
  • Wind and temperature vary according to the selected Monte Carlo mode.
  • A mission is considered successful only if energy required does not exceed usable battery energy after reserve.
  • The model reports missions per charge and deliveries per full charge using average mission energy and average usable capacity.

docs.title: Question(s) Answered
docs.text:
• Can the battery complete the mission while maintaining reserve?
  • How many deliveries can be completed per charge?
  • How much reserve margin remains after mission completion?

docs.title: Primary Variables
docs.text:
• Battery Configuration
  • Payload Weight
  • Flight Distance
  • Ambient Temperature
  • Wind Speed

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Monte Carlo analysis
  • Run repeated randomized mission trials for each battery candidate
  • Compare mission energy demand against effective capacity after reserve
  • Aggregate results across all trials

docs.title: Outputs / Acceptance Evidence
docs.text:
• Mission success probability
  • Average energy used per mission (Wh)
  • Missions per charge
  • Deliveries per charge
  • Remaining energy distribution
  • Comparative battery performance under nominal and extreme conditions

docs.title: Validation Data Source
docs.text:
• End-to-end simulation behavior
  • Internal consistency checks
  • Comparison of expected depletion behavior versus model output

docs.title: Analysis Deliverable
docs.text:
• Mission success summary by battery
  • Table/chart of missions per charge
  • Comparison of remaining energy distributions across batteries

docs.title: Requirement
docs.text: The model shall compare candidate battery configurations and determine which configuration provides better mission margin and missions-per-charge performance under common operating conditions.

docs.title: Assumptions / Constraints
docs.text:
• All battery candidates are evaluated using the same mission/environment input framework.
  • The drone platform is assumed constant:
  • empty drone weight = 50 lb
  • same mission speed and reserve threshold
  • Chemistry differences are represented through battery parameters, including:
  • nominal capacity
  • baseline power draw
  • payload penalty
  • wind penalty
  • cold-capacity penalty
  • cold-power penalty
  • The current model compares battery candidates for mission performance, but does not yet implement recharge-cycle degradation or true end-of-life lifecycle modeling.

docs.title: Question(s) Answered
docs.text:
• Which battery retains more post-mission energy?
  • Which battery supports more missions per charge?
  • How do candidate batteries differ under nominal and extreme conditions?

docs.title: Primary Variables
docs.text: • Battery Candidate / Battery Configuration

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Monte Carlo analysis
  • Execute the same set of randomized mission trials for each battery candidate
  • Compare aggregated summary statistics between batteries

docs.title: Outputs / Acceptance Evidence
docs.text:
• Mean remaining energy (%)
  • 5th and 95th percentile remaining energy
  • Average mission energy use (Wh)
  • Missions per charge
  • Success rate
  • Delta comparison between candidate batteries

docs.title: Validation Data Source
docs.text:
• Battery specification assumptions
  • Comparative simulation results
  • Engineering review of parameter realism

docs.title: Analysis Deliverable
docs.text:
• Comparison chart/table per battery:
  • average remaining energy
  • percentile bands
  • average Wh per mission
  • missions per charge
  • success rate
  • Nominal vs extreme comparison summary

docs.title: FUTURE-REQ — Trips Before Battery End-of-Life (EOL)
docs.text:
The current model does not yet implement true battery lifecycle degradation across recharge cycles. A future enhancement should add: - cycle-dependent battery degradation - capacity fade over recharge count - performance degradation versus age/use - total trips before battery end-of-life

This would support a future requirement such as:

The model shall determine the total number of trips achievable for each candidate battery before end-of-life (EOL) using a lifecycle degradation model.

docs.title: Requirements Traceability
docs.text: Requirement Primary Variable Method Validation Source Key Output REQ-001 Payload, distance, temperature, wind, battery configuration Monte Carlo mission simulation Battery test data, engineering assumptions Energy used per mission, remaining energy, success/failure REQ-002 Battery configuration under variable operating conditions Monte Carlo mission feasibility analysis End-to-end simulation, depletion consistency checks Success rate, missions per charge, deliveries per charge REQ-003 Battery candidate / configuration Monte Carlo battery comparison Comparative engineering review Remaining energy distribution, Wh per mission, missions per charge FUTURE-REQ Battery lifecycle / recharge degradation Future lifecycle Monte Carlo extension Life cycle test data Trips before EOL

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The current model explicitly assumes a 50 lb empty drone weight.
  • The model currently evaluates single-mission performance and charge-level mission throughput.
  • The model does not yet calculate long-term battery EOL unless lifecycle degradation logic is added.
  • Battery chemistry is represented indirectly through configuration parameters rather than a standalone chemistry equation.
